title: When should an air sensor be checked again?
person: A researcher maintaining inexpensive environmental sensors.
problem: A cheap sensor can gradually become less accurate; checking it against a reference instrument has a cost.
everyday_example: A sensor becomes less accurate over several weeks. Compare when a model requests new reference readings, and whether those readings reduce future error. This cannot establish why the sensor changed.
scientific_question: At equal budgets of newly revealed reference measurements, which sequential recalibration policy best controls future concentration error and worst-week error on a changing sensor time series?
model_training_or_adaptation: Fit ridge and shallow boosted-tree calibration models, then learn a small residual-update model. Compare scheduled, uncertainty-based and drift-triggered label requests; explicitly charge every reference reading used.
baselines_and_comparisons: Static ridge; static boosted trees
Periodic recalibration and random measurement requests at the same label budget
Rolling-window retraining; uncertainty-only selection; proposed combined disagreement-and-change trigger
leakage_aware_evaluation: Chronological outer blocks; tune thresholds only on earlier months. Mask all unpurchased reference values. Fit imputers/scalers only on historical training data. Group uncertainty estimates by week; report MAE, worst-week MAE, error versus purchased labels, and update time. Report performance under changing conditions without attributing causal contributions to sensor drift or concentration changes; this dataset cannot identify them.

data_access.access_proof: UCI CSV prefix parsed: 303 complete rows, 15 columns; sensor and reference fields present.
data_access.licence: UCI currently displays CC BY 4.0; embedded historical terms restrict use to research and exclude commercial use. Proposed thesis stays within the intersection.
data_access.uncertainty: One historic outdoor installation, 2004–2005; no indoor, multi-device or modern regulatory claim. Do not transfer the thesis data into a venture without resolving the terms.

cpu_plan: Pilot: 2,000 chronological rows, ridge/tree fits, at most 20 parameter settings. Full dataset about 9,358 rows; laptop memory target below 2 GB. Measure actual time in the pilot; no runtime measured today. VPS optional for result viewing, not training.
multi_month_scope: Weeks 1–3: reproduce static calibration and audit missing sentinel -200
Weeks 4–8: build the budgeted sequential learning protocol and implement three update policies
Weeks 9–14: nested chronological evaluation, seasonal stress tests and ablations
Weeks 15–20: sensitivity/uncertainty analysis, reproducible package and thesis
closest_work: The October 2026 lightweight indoor-calibration study already evaluates drift and chronological deployment scenarios. Its newly described dataset access was not verified here; use UCI data only. Public LinkedIn calibration webinars corroborate professional interest, not demand.
proposed_difference: Compare sequential update and measurement-request policies at exactly matched reference-label budgets on a public historical dataset. Existing reference-efficient and drift-aware calibration methods are baselines; this is an applied comparative study, not a newly invented calibration principle.
risks: One device limits external validity
Missing references and seasonality can bias query policy comparisons
Acquisition cost is simulated; no actual instrument cost or field savings claimed
concrete_output: An auditable sequential calibration benchmark, trained compact models, label-budget/error curves and a recommendation about when simple schedules suffice.
verdict_reason: Public research-compatible data, small CPU workload and a substantive adaptive-learning comparison. LTU connection is a measurement/efficient-ML methods fit, not a currently advertised air-sensor thesis.

title: Tell a water engineer when several leak locations look equally plausible
person: A researcher testing water-network diagnosis methods.
problem: A few pressure sensors may not identify a unique leaking pipe, especially when two leaks occur together.
everyday_example: The same pressure drop could come from either of two streets. The study tests whether a model should return a small region rather than one confident pipe.
scientific_question: In a public simulated water network, how do sensor loss, concurrent leaks and hydraulic-model mismatch change the size and reliability of a learned set of possible leak locations?
model_training_or_adaptation: Generate labelled hydraulic scenarios from the verified public network. Train a small graph classifier or gradient-boosted residual classifier and calibrate location sets; compare single-location and set-valued predictions. For unseen locations, use shared node-wise graph scores or scenario matching. A fixed multiclass boosted-tree model is only a known-location baseline.
baselines_and_comparisons: Pressure-residual nearest scenario and hydraulic sensitivity ranking
Boosted trees on sensor residuals
Small graph model with/without physical residuals; current physics-informed GNN as a conceptual comparator
leakage_aware_evaluation: Split entire simulated episodes and leak locations, not adjacent time steps. Hold out demand patterns, roughness perturbations and leak pairs. Report coverage versus graph-distance/region size and false localization on no-leak episodes. Any conformal-style coverage is empirical under model shift, not a guaranteed field bound. Report known-location episode generalization separately from unseen-node tests; only models capable of scoring unseen nodes enter the latter comparison.

title: Stop sleep-stage smoothing from erasing short real changes
person: A sleep-signal researcher checking automatic overnight scoring.
problem: Making predictions look smoother can improve average accuracy while deleting short bouts that the human scorer actually marked.
everyday_example: A scorer marks one minute of waking between longer sleep periods. A smoother may erase it as noise; the study asks when that helps and when it hides evidence.
scientific_question: Can a compact learned smoothing gate improve macro-F1 without materially reducing recall of human-labelled short stage bouts, compared with fixed-duration and confidence-aware smoothing?
model_training_or_adaptation: Use YASA as a task-specific pretrained LightGBM baseline, plus a locally trained feature classifier. Train a small gate deciding whether to accept an epoch prediction or a smoothed alternative using local probabilities and signal-quality features.
baselines_and_comparisons: Unsmoothed epoch classifier; majority/median smoothing
HMM/HSMM duration smoothing
StageGuard-style confidence/quality-aware smoothing; random-transformer smoother where reproducible
leakage_aware_evaluation: Group all nights by person. Tune on development people, test once on held-out people; disclose potential pretrained data exposure. Report macro-F1, transition precision/recall, duration-stratified bout recall and temporal displacement. Score 30-second labels only: no claim to identify micro-arousals absent in annotations. YASA uses future context, so compare offline scoring at matched context windows.

data_access.access_proof: Sleep-EDF public signal EDF prefix parsed; full 4,620-byte hypnogram fetched and sleep labels parsed.
data_access.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License 1.0 on PhysioNet; not CC BY.
data_access.uncertainty: Full nights were not downloaded. Historical cohorts and scorer labels do not establish clinical benefit; check model/software terms before redistributing weights.

cpu_plan: Pilot: four to eight nights, cached epoch features and tiny gate; process EDF in chunks, target below 4 GB RAM. Scale to a participant-stratified subset of 20–40 people before deciding whether all nights are necessary.
multi_month_scope: Weeks 1–3: validate epochs, stages and participant grouping
Weeks 4–8: reproduce unsmoothed/fixed and current quality-aware alternatives
Weeks 9–14: train gate, compare equal context and test duration sensitivities
Weeks 15–20: ablate signal quality versus confidence, quantify uncertainty and write
closest_work: StageGuard (July 2026) already combines transition constraints, duration models and signal quality. October duration-aware world-model work and May random-transformer research make generic learned smoothing a weak novelty claim. AnySleep (October 30) addresses broad channel-agnostic staging at a very different training scale.
proposed_difference: An applied failure-analysis and mitigation project centred on preserving labelled short bouts under a fixed computation/context budget. A careful negative result against simple/current smoothers is legitimate; superiority is not promised.
risks: Gate may reproduce StageGuard rather than add useful behaviour
Few short bouts yield wide intervals
Sleep EDF label conventions and cohorts limit generalization

title: Should an ECG model fill missing signals or work with what it has?
person: A researcher building robust ECG analysis models.
problem: Reconstructed ECG channels can look plausible while changing the classification result.
everyday_example: Two recorded ECG lead channels are unavailable. Compare rebuilding those signals with telling the classifier which channels are missing. This does not simulate the physical effects of electrode failure.
scientific_question: At a matched CPU/model budget, when does direct mask-aware multi-label classification outperform reconstruction-then-classification under missing ECG leads and time segments?
model_training_or_adaptation: Train a compact 1-D CNN at 100 Hz with observed-signal masks and structured lead dropout. Compare linear/compact autoencoder reconstruction followed by the same classifier. Learn calibration on held-out patients.
baselines_and_comparisons: Zero-fill plus missingness mask; fixed surviving-lead classifier
Linear cross-lead regression and small denoising autoencoder
Direct structured-dropout classifier; ImputeECG as the current high-compute reconstruction reference, not a promised reproduction
leakage_aware_evaluation: Use PTB-XL v1.0.3 patient-wise folds 1–8/9/10, with duplicate audit. Mask leads/time windows only after splitting. Evaluate macro-AUPRC, label-wise sensitivity at preselected specificity, calibration and risk/coverage. Separate random failures from lead-specific structured loss. Synthetic missingness is not evidence about a clinic’s actual failure process.

data_access.access_proof: Public PTB-XL metadata prefix parsed, complete waveform header read, and full 24,000-byte 100-Hz 12-lead ECG record decoded.
data_access.uncertainty: No institutional credentials/new agreement required for these files. Clinical deployment, patient benefit and external-hospital validity are not established.

cpu_plan: Pilot: 1,000–2,000 records, five diagnostic superclasses, less than 500k parameters, short early-stopped runs. Stream batches; target under 6 GB RAM. Expand only after measuring wall time; no A100 replication or 500-Hz transformer training.
multi_month_scope: Weeks 1–3: validate labels, folds and signal scaling
Weeks 4–8: train matched compact baselines
Weeks 9–14: structured missingness and direct-versus-reconstruction ablations
Weeks 15–20: calibration, subgroup uncertainty, compute profile and thesis

proposed_difference: An equal-budget applied comparison of directly learned missingness handling against reconstruction, including where visually good reconstruction harms decisions. Downstream diagnostic evaluation itself is not new.
risks: July closest work is outside the desired 90-day corroboration window; no invented fresh trigger
Full-waveform public labels are coarse
Missingness simulation cannot prove safety of reconstructed signals

title: Teach a small model when an empty form field is for a signature
plain_problem: An empty signature line and an ordinary text field can look almost identical. The clue is often beside the field: its label, neighbouring date field or place in the form.
example: A form contains two blank underlined regions. One is a postal address and one is a signature. A crop of the blank line alone loses the information needed to tell them apart.
outcome: A trained compact context model, a reproducible test of which surrounding evidence matters, and an explicit account of accuracy versus CPU cost. This is field-type recognition given candidate regions, not a claim to solve complete document extraction.
why_this_topic_now: Started from LTU’s current Form Field Extraction project, then its September 2026 mini-CommonForms paper. The paper reports severe signature-class weakness and describes text/signature confusion. The proposed question isolates context and imbalance instead of repeating its detector comparison.
ai_question: At equal training examples and parameter/CPU budgets, does learning the relation between an empty field and its surroundings improve signature-versus-text classification on unseen form families more than larger crops or class balancing alone? Does any gain survive perturbation of the candidate boundary?

learning_method.train: Train from scratch a small shared CNN with two views: field crop and an expanded context crop with the field location marked. Fuse the embeddings with relative geometry; compare simple concatenation against a learned gate. Use 96–128 pixel crops and a target below one million parameters. No LLM or paid model calls.
learning_method.adaptation: Class-balanced minibatches and a contrastive/margin term for confusing signature/text pairs. Keep loss weighting, context radius and feature fusion as separately tested factors.
learning_method.scope_limit: Primary endpoint is conditional field-type classification using provided boxes. Add deterministic line/rectangle candidates as a secondary operational test only after measuring their proposal recall; never report oracle-box accuracy as detector accuracy.

title: Keep marginal notes separate when manuscript training labels are rough
plain_problem: A digitisation model must separate main text from marginal notes. Precise pixel labels are expensive; coarse boundaries can teach a model to erase small notes or merge them into the main text.
example: A narrow handwritten comment touches the main text. Enlarging its training mask by a few pixels may swallow surrounding strokes; an ordinary segmentation loss then treats this approximation as unquestionable truth.
outcome: A compact segmentation model trained to tolerate a controlled amount of boundary uncertainty, plus evidence about which label approximations preserve small marginal notes across manuscripts.
why_this_topic_now: Started from LTU’s current Page Layout Analysis work explicitly distinguishing main text and marginalia, corroborated by the 26 October 2026 project update and a document-analysis project beginning 1 November 2026. Public DIVA-HisDB is the experimental instrument, not a new dataset claim.
ai_question: For a fixed small segmentation network and page budget, can an uncertainty-aware boundary loss retain marginalia under coarsened training masks better than hard labels, ignored boundary bands or standard label smoothing, without degrading clean-label performance? How much transfers to a held-out manuscript?

learning_method.train: Train a compact L-U-Net-inspired or narrow U-Net from scratch using 256x256 tiles, with main text/comment/decoration/background targets. A roughly 65k-parameter L-U-Net is described in the closest weak-label paper; the actual implementation and parameter count must be checked.
learning_method.adaptation: Create controlled label approximations only in training: polygon simplification and class-wise erosion/dilation with a fixed scale normalised by page resolution. Assign boundary pixels a set of plausible adjacent classes, preserve confident interior supervision, and add consistency between two image perturbations.
learning_method.control: Compare set-valued boundary loss with simply ignoring the same band, matched soft-label smoothing, and hard noisy masks. Do not mix boundary noise with missing-whole-region labels in the primary experiment. Optional missing-note stress test is separately reported.
learning_method.claim_limit: Synthetic coarsening measures tolerance to specified label defects. It does not prove human annotation-time savings, expert disagreement or restoration of historically correct text.

evaluation.splits: No tiles or augmentations from a page cross folds. Primary protocol uses official training/validation/test identities within each manuscript. evaluation.person_control: Writer/person identities are not verified in the available release. Do not call a within-manuscript result writer-independent. Whole-manuscript holdout provides a stronger style/source separation but only three sources; cannot support population-wide writer-generalisation claims.
evaluation.metrics: Comment-class IoU and F1, macro-IoU excluding background, boundary F-score at specified pixel tolerance, connected-component split/merge counts, and recall of small comment components. Report clean-label accuracy drop and worst-manuscript result. Component size bins fixed from training data.
evaluation.statistics: Resample pages, never pixels, for within-manuscript intervals; report each held-out manuscript separately. Three final seeds. All noise seeds, radii and label-generation rules fixed before test evaluation.
evaluation.ablations: Noise type and radius, 2/5/10 training pages per manuscript if masks support it, interior supervision versus consistency term, class balance, context tile size, fixed parameter and training-time budgets.

Weeks 4–6: deterministic label coarsening, page-level evaluation and clean/noisy controls.

Weeks 11–14: fixed-budget ablations and held-out-manuscript experiments.
Weeks 15–20: error taxonomy, uncertainty/limitations, reproducibility and thesis writing.
contribution: A trained noise-tolerant layout method with a reproducible map of failure thresholds for rare semantic regions; a controlled evaluation separating label uncertainty, small-region loss and manuscript shift.
risks: Three manuscripts severely limit generalisation; no invented independent-writer count.
Morphological mask defects are controlled simulations, not measured human annotation behaviour.
Label palette/bit encoding must be verified before interpreting classes; RGB channels are not assumed to be direct class IDs.
Small tiles may remove needed layout context; include a fixed context-size control.
Large clean-label differences or identical performance to ignored boundaries could defeat the proposed method; a sound negative comparison is still a valid smaller research result.
venture_hypothesis: Potential later application is reducing rework in archival digitisation. No archive partnership, buyer demand or annotation-effort saving established.
